name: RoboLink CoDrone EDU
description: A 54.8g caged quadcopter from Robolink built for real dual-language programming: Blockly for Robolink block coding progressing to genuine Python via the official `codrone-edu` package. Carries 7+ onboard sensors (accelerometer, gyroscope, barometer, front and bottom time-of-flight range sensors, optical flow, dual RGB color sensors) but no camera. Controlled over a proprietary 2.4GHz RF link — not Bluetooth or Wi-Fi — via an included physical Smart Controller with its own telemetry LCD, supporting up to 10 drones flying simultaneously without interference. Marketed for grades 6-10 (ages 12+), used as the official drone in REC Foundation's Aerial Drone Competition.

specs.label: Battery
specs.note: ~60min charge via a dual charger; 2 batteries ship per kit

specs.label: Weight
specs.note: with battery installed, drone only; well under the FAA's 250g registration threshold — per Robolink's official spec sheet

specs.label: Dimensions
specs.note: 138.8 × 138.5 × 34.8mm per Robolink's official spec sheet; drone only, excludes the included Smart Controller

specs.label: Connectivity
specs.note: not Bluetooth or Wi-Fi — the discontinued 2016-era CoDrone Pro/Lite predecessor used Bluetooth 4.0, a common source of confusion; supports 10 drones flying simultaneously, ~50m line-of-sight range

specs.label: Sensors
specs.note: accelerometer, gyroscope, barometer, front + bottom time-of-flight range sensors, optical flow (position hold), dual RGB color sensors, temperature; camera arrives only on the unreleased CoDrone EDU Plus, not this model

specs.label: Software
specs.note: official `codrone-edu` PyPI package; Scratch and Swift Playgrounds are both explicitly listed as unsupported by Robolink's own compatibility docs, despite being commonly assumed

specs.label: Controller
specs.note: 128x64 telemetry LCD, 4 programmable RGB LEDs, powered by 2 AA batteries or Micro-USB; tablets are explicitly not compatible since the system needs a wired computer connection

specs.label: Propeller Cage
specs.note: color-coded red/black props for CW/CCW pairing

specs.label: Calculator Support
specs.note: a Texas Instruments partnership lets students program the drone directly from a graphing calculator

specs.label: Age/Grade
specs.note: REC Foundation's Aerial Drone Competition, which uses this drone, spans grades 4-12 more broadly

specs.label: Indoor Safety
specs.note: under the 250g threshold, exempt from Remote ID; FAA rules generally don't apply to purely indoor flight, which is how this product is designed to be used

sourcing: Specs and history compiled from Robolink's own product page, technical specification sheet, and compatibility/help documentation, the `codrone-edu` PyPI package listing and its linked GitHub repositories, Robolink's Kickstarter campaign pages (2016 and 2022), REC Foundation partnership announcements, a Texas Instruments integration announcement, and independent reviews (The Drone Girl, EDGEucating, STEM Kit Review) plus an REC Foundation best-practices document on classroom drone durability. Several details are flagged as unconfirmed above: the specific open-source license (if any) covering Robolink's public GitHub repos, and the precise legal status of a classroom teacher's FAA recreational-flyer classification versus Part 107 requirements, which wasn't fully resolved in available sources. This entry hasn't yet been cross-linked into the rest of the Classroom & Coding Kits subcategory or synced to the directory listing; that's planned for a later pass.

pricing.summary: A single CoDrone EDU kit runs **$249.00** direct from Robolink, with classroom bundles scaling from a **$3,599** 12-pack up to a **$5,399** 18-pack. Professional-development training is sold as a separate add-on, not bundled into these base classroom prices.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: This catalog withholds an Open Source badge because although Robolink publishes the drone's Python SDK and Blockly code publicly (via GitHub and PyPI), none of those repos carries a clear license file — so "source is public" is confirmed but "open-source-licensed" isn't, and the flight-controller firmware itself remains closed. It also connects over a proprietary 2.4GHz RF link rather than Bluetooth, despite Bluetooth being commonly assumed from the earlier, discontinued CoDrone Pro/Lite.

firmwareCommunity.note: Robolink's official Python SDK source for CoDrone EDU, also published to PyPI as the codrone-edu package; the specific open-source license covering the repo isn't clearly stated.
